developments.title: HD Moore's canary study uncovers three compromised AI service providers
detail: A study by security researcher HD Moore seeded two million canary prompts into popular AI services and monitored where the data was exfiltrated.
The investigation identified three compromised providers, resellers that stole prompts via built‑in logging, and providers that ignored Zero Data Retention (ZDR) and privacy flags.
Following the report, Vercel's AI Gateway team deployed a similar canary‑monitoring setup as a backup for their own providers.
developments.why_it_matters: AI service operators must audit logging and enforce ZDR policies to stop prompt leakage and protect user privacy.

developments.title: Vocab Surgery suppresses Inkling-2-Mini refusals through token-weight edits
detail: Pliny the Liberator reports that “Vocab Surgery” changed Inkling-2-Mini's embedding and unembedding matrices without retraining or altering the model's attention, MLP, router, or normalization layers. The method shifted seven refusal-token embeddings 90% toward compliance counterparts and scaled those tokens plus three safety tokens down to 10% of their original unembedding weight. Across more than 800 prompts, Pliny reports a near-zero refusal rate with negligible capability loss. He says the process took less than two minutes on a MacBook.
developments.why_it_matters: Vocab Surgery gives model evaluators a no-retraining way to isolate vocabulary weighting from broader model changes.

developments.title: GitHub adds pull-request restrictions based on submitter account age or merged history
detail: GitHub maintainers can now restrict pull requests based on a submitter’s account age or merged pull-request history.

Will McGugan says he disabled pull requests on the Rich and Textual projects after an influx of low-quality contributions, many from developers using AI or unattended agents, and notes that the blanket disable also blocks some high-quality human and AI pull requests.
developments.why_it_matters: Maintainers can now apply submitter-history gates instead of disabling pull requests entirely.

developments.title: Gemini Neon reportedly reaches No. 1 on LiveBench
detail: Matt Van Horn reports that Google’s Gemini Neon reached No. 1 in an AI_Screening LiveBench result. He also describes a Gemini Neon rap song and music video built around reactions to the model’s benchmark performance.
developments.why_it_matters: LLM evaluations should include Terminal-Bench, because Matt Van Horn reports that Opus still leads that benchmark by half a point.

developments.title: Dots desktop agent can connect to a PC but cannot list local Codex threads
detail: Kevin reports that the Dots assistant connected through a desktop app and showed the PC as connected, but it could not view the local Codex thread list because Windows denied desktop access.
The exchange demonstrates that a successful desktop-app connection does not by itself grant the assistant permission to enumerate Codex threads on the host.
developments.why_it_matters: Readers using Dots to inspect Codex threads should not assume connected status means the assistant can view those threads on Windows.

developments.title: Ohya's SQL-mode MCP tool queries agent session logs, with reported savings over grep and transcript-based recall
detail: Ohya exposes a single MCP tool that runs in SQL mode over agent session logs, synchronizing history across devices with Tailcat and storing it in SQLite so agents can retrieve past interactions through MCP or a command-line interface without re-executing prior tool calls.

Against a baseline of an agent grepping the same logs, the tool is reported to save 33%, though the supplied evidence does not specify whether that figure refers to tokens, wall-clock time, or cost, and gives no benchmark methodology or supported log formats.
A separate head-to-head test against Atuin threads and raw transcripts reportedly completed 20% faster, required 38% fewer tool calls, and produced 62% less output.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers evaluating agent memory tooling can now weigh SQL-mode log queries against grep- and transcript-based recall when choosing how agents retrieve past sessions.

developments.title: Inbox adds generic MCP support for email, Linear, and Sentry workflows
detail: Greg Pstrucha reports that his Inbox project now supports MCP as a generic protocol for integrations, replacing point-to-point Gmail wiring with a single connection pattern. After connecting it to executor, Inbox can turn items from email, Linear, and similar sources into free-form items, with future sources such as Sentry alerts also possible.
He notes that automation UX still needs work, while the MCP layer removes integration-specific effort and lets him concentrate on filtering and prioritizing incoming items.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers can add new sources like Sentry alerts without writing a custom integration for each service.

developments.title: Ghostscript's reported Upload2Shell flaw enables image-upload RCE
detail: Alexey Fateev reports that pwn.ai's Upload2Shell exploit targets CVE-2026-125396, a Ghostscript Type 1 font-loader flaw that escapes the -dSAFER sandbox. Crafted PNG or JPEG files containing EPS content can reportedly execute code when processed by ImageMagick or Pillow.

The reported path reaches Gradio 6.32.0 through gr.Image, which launches gs -dSAFER before Python runs, and potentially affects ComfyUI, AUTOMATIC1111, InvokeAI, and Home Assistant when their Pillow upload paths use Ghostscript. Fateev also reports confirmed shells against Google's image renderer, Roundcube, Debian 13 CUPS, and WordPress Core, with the Google renderer fixed on November 10. The stated mitigation is to check gs --version and update Ghostscript to 10.08.0 or uninstall it.
developments.why_it_matters: Administrators should inventory and patch every Ghostscript-backed upload path now, because one vulnerable library can expose otherwise unrelated web and AI applications to the same execution path.

developments.title: Hy4 vision model added to Ollama Cloud
detail: Ollama Cloud now hosts Hy4, the latest model from Tencent Hunyuan. The model contains 770 billion parameters with 49 billion active per token and is the first Hy series model to support vision and computer use.

The service runs in the United States and guarantees zero data retention, providing a privacy‑preserving environment for multimodal tasks such as image analysis, frontend development, and finance research. Users can start the model with the command `ollama run hy4:cloud`.
developments.why_it_matters: You can now run vision‑enabled AI via Ollama Cloud without any data being stored, enabling private multimodal workloads.

developments.title: Sakana AI pretrains its Sakana Sawara language model from scratch for agent use
detail: Sakana AI chief scientist Takuya Akiba introduced Sakana Sawara, a language model pretrained from scratch and built with agent workloads in mind.
He frames LLM development as an intensely competitive research race, saying progress hinges on compute resources multiplied by research efficiency and on dense teams of strong researchers.
Akiba also describes a "partial RSI" loop in which Sawara itself helps accelerate development of the next Sawara generation.
developments.why_it_matters: Readers choosing base models for agent pipelines now have an independently pretrained option from Sakana AI, not a continuation of an existing checkpoint.

developments.title: ZAI releases GLM-5.4 with vision capabilities and 50% higher token quota
detail: ZAI announced GLM-5.4 for all users of the GLM Coding Plan; it adds vision capabilities and increases token quota by 50% compared with GLM-5.3. Some reports describe it as a Loop Transformer-based model, while community observations about that architecture switch and a possible GLM-5.5 remain unconfirmed. A user also demonstrated generating two WebGL2 photon-tracer renderers from scratch, producing thousands of shader lines without external dependencies.
developments.why_it_matters: This gives developers a larger image-capable context window inside the existing GLM Coding Plan.

developments.title: Opentrawl Agentic OS Search Tool Announced
detail: A sneak‑preview was posted for Opentrawl, a new agentic operating‑system component that lets users search their entire digital life from any device. The tool offers end‑to‑end encryption and is released as open‑source software.

Opentrawl can be deployed on a user's own infrastructure at no cost, or run as a paid cloud service where data remains encrypted in RAM. This flexibility aims to give individuals control over their personal data while providing cloud convenience.
developments.why_it_matters: You can now self‑host a fully encrypted personal search assistant, reducing reliance on third‑party services.

developments.title: Reframe360 MCP Server and CLI Enables Automated Insta360 Video Reframing
detail: The reframe360 repository provides an MCP server and command‑line interface that automatically reframes raw Insta360 360° dual‑fisheye video using the camera’s 1000 Hz IMU data and exports to DaVinci Resolve Fusion.
Built on Gemini Neon’s agentic MCP framework, the tool removes the need for the Insta360 Studio application and manual keyframe adjustments, streamlining the video editing workflow.
developments.why_it_matters: You can now reframe raw Insta360 dual‑fisheye footage automatically with a single command, eliminating manual keyframe editing and saving hours of post‑production work.

external_links.title: GitHub - joshp123/reframe360: MCP server and CLI for reframing raw Insta360 360° dual-fisheye video with 1000 Hz IMU horizon lock and DaVinci Resolve Fusion export · GitHub

developments.title: OpenAI releases “Perplexity and Intelligence” essay proposing safety limits
detail: OpenAI published an essay titled “Perplexity and Intelligence” that outlines shared safety limits for AI pretraining based on perplexity measurements.
The essay argues that progress beyond these limits should be gated on the ability to understand AI behavior, aiming to establish common safety bars across the community.
developments.why_it_matters: Researchers can now benchmark their models against OpenAI’s proposed perplexity limits, ensuring safety thresholds are met before further scaling.

developments.title: Maziyar Panahi trains simulated hospital robot to catch IV lines in 83 minutes on a single GPU
detail: Maziyar Panahi trained a hospital robot policy whose task is to catch an IV line before it yanks the cannula out, arguing that hospital robots must be safety-capable rather than intelligent to matter clinically. The policy was trained across 4,096 simulated hospital beds running in parallel, with total training taking 83 minutes on a single GPU.

In 1,024 held-out simulated episodes, the untrained policy caught the line 0 times while the trained policy succeeded 919 times, and the trained policy held median peak pull at the cannula to 0.6 newtons.
developments.why_it_matters: Robotics teams can judge hospital robot policies by measured IV-line catch rate and cannula pull force, not general model intelligence.

developments.title: Vercel ships Board as a private Slack workspace for AI agents and developers
detail: Vercel Board is a shipped workspace that behaves like a private Slack environment shared by AI agents and human developers, giving each participant its own identity and the ability to sync activity to Slack channels for observability.
Matt Pocock describes using it for collaborative grilling, where an agent or developer can ping the other—or the other's agent—directly from the board.
developments.why_it_matters: Teams can adopt Vercel Board to give agents and developers a shared private workspace with per-participant identities and Slack channel sync for observability.

developments.title: OpenCode 2.4.0 adds automations triggered by schedule or MCP events
detail: OpenCode 2.4.0 includes a new automation tool that lets agents create automations running on a schedule or reacting to MCP events.
Those automations can trigger prompts, shell commands, or a code-mode script that can access connected MCP tools.
dax describes using such an automation to monitor email through an existing MCP connection, handle later instructions, purchase a domain, and set up Cloudflare.
developments.why_it_matters: OpenCode users can now delegate recurring or event-driven tasks to automations that invoke prompts, shell commands, or MCP-aware scripts instead of manually triggering each step.

developments.title: Unsloth reports 125 tokens/s for Inkling 2 Mini on RTX Pro 6000
detail: Unsloth reports that Inkling 2 Mini GGUF inference now runs about 1.9 times faster locally, reaching 125 tokens per second on an NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000.
The updated path is available through Unsloth Desktop; Unsloth's GitHub project provides a local interface for running LLMs, and its Hugging Face repository hosts the Inkling 2 Mini GGUF files.
developments.why_it_matters: Inkling 2 Mini GGUF users can switch to Unsloth Desktop for higher-throughput local serving on an NVIDIA RTX Pro 6000 without a reported accuracy tradeoff.

external_links.title: GitHub - unslothai/unsloth: Local UI to run and train LLMs and diffusion models. Supports GGUF, MLX, Qwen3.8, DeepSeek-V4.1, MiniMax-H3, Gemma 4, FLUX and more. · GitHub

developments.title: Inkling 2 Mini variable-loop runs achieve 92.6% accuracy with shorter answers
detail: Maziyar Panahi reported running the variable-loop variant of Inkling 2 Mini on a set of 1,273 medical exam questions, testing loop counts from 1 to 5.

The results show a jump from 86.6% accuracy at 1 loop to 92.1% at 2 loops—a 70‑question reduction in errors—and a modest further increase to 92.6% at 5 loops while the generated answers become 34% shorter.
These findings build on NDIF’s hosting of Inkling 2 Mini and the provided guide for steering model activations across loops.
developments.why_it_matters: Use variable-loop processing to improve model accuracy and cut output length, saving inference time and token costs.

developments.title: Gemini subscription access is restricted to Antigravity; T3 Code is currently allowed through the Antigravity binary
detail: Google's Gemini subscription is now restricted to Antigravity, according to Theo. T3 Code remains usable because it invokes the Antigravity binary before reaching Google's API, while Pi's fake Antigravity shim is not allowed. Dan McAteer reports running Gemini 4 Neon through T3 Code under that arrangement. Logan says the T3 Code path is expected to change soon.
developments.why_it_matters: Developers using Gemini in third-party coding harnesses must ensure their tool routes through Antigravity or expect access to be revoked.

developments.title: Factory Droid becomes available in Google Chat spaces and direct messages
detail: Factory announced that its Droid agent is now available in Google Chat. Users can mention Factory in a space or send it a direct message containing the task, repository, and criteria for checking the result. Droid begins the work, posts progress in the thread, and replies when finished.
developments.why_it_matters: Teams using Google Chat can delegate coding tasks without switching tools, with progress updates posted in the same thread.

developments.title: Braintrust launches generalized observability agent
detail: Braintrust has launched its generalized observability agent, built on the Brainstore database, marking the first public release of the product after a month of development.
The agent ingests any structured or unstructured telemetry and extracts useful signals without being limited to specific data shapes or problem classes.
developments.why_it_matters: You can now route all telemetry through one agent instead of building custom integrations, streamlining observability pipelines and speeding insight delivery.

developments.title: Dinkus and Ishmael support progressive Shift-based text selection
detail: Will McGugan reports that Dinkus implements a “tap-to-select” feature. Pressing Shift selects a word, and pressing it again expands the selection through punctuation-delimited clauses, then sentences, and finally the document.
He says Ishmael also includes the feature, with a more sophisticated implementation that understands dialog punctuation.
developments.why_it_matters: Dinkus and Ishmael users can select exact text ranges with repeated Shift presses, removing the mouse requirement for selection.

developments.title: Conductor adds Usage dashboard for chats, tokens, and estimated cost by model and workspace
detail: Charlie Holtz announced a new Usage feature in Conductor. The dashboard shows chats, estimated cost, and token counts across local workspaces for the last 90 days.
The usage data can be broken down both by model and by workspace, giving users visibility into how their token consumption and estimated spend are distributed.
developments.why_it_matters: You can now audit chat volume, tokens, and estimated cost per workspace and per model over 90 days, and spot which workspace or model drives your spend.

developments.title: Dan McAteer introduces Hippo, a lightweight agent memory system for Obsidian and markdown file systems
detail: Dan McAteer is testing Hippo (short for hippocampus), a homebrewed, ultra-lightweight agent memory system.

The system follows the principles laid out in Anthropic's recent "Components of agent memory" article, and McAteer reports it has been a major unlock for working with multiple agents across different vendors.
It can be installed for Obsidian or any markdown-based file system by pointing an agent at the repository.
developments.why_it_matters: Agent users running Obsidian or another markdown-based file system can point their agent at the repo to get memory that works across multiple agents and vendors.

developments.title: Maziyar Panahi finds longer thinking drops an open reasoning model to 56–64% accuracy on 1,273 medical exam questions
detail: Maziyar Panahi ran an open reasoning model three times across 1,273 medical exam questions and tracked accuracy against thinking length. Under 1K thinking tokens the model was 99% correct on every run, but past 8K tokens accuracy fell to a range of 56% to 64%.
Panahi reads a long reasoning trace as the model signaling it is lost, and recommends surfacing how long the model thought to clinicians alongside each answer.
developments.why_it_matters: Clinicians can use thinking-token count as a triage signal, routing any answer that exceeded 8K thinking tokens — accuracy 56% to 64% — to human review.

developments.title: fxs tool launches Vercel Sandbox for parallel AI agents
detail: Pranit introduced fxs, a command-line tool that spins up a Vercel Sandbox from a warm snapshot, runs AI agents (fx, Claude, Codex, Opencode) with preconfigured skills and MCPs, syncs session data back to the local disk, and automatically stops when idle.
The tool enables developers to run dozens of agent sessions concurrently without taxing their local machine, allowing workflows with 50+ parallel sessions.
By offloading builds and tests to the sandbox, users retain their local workflow while leveraging cloud resources.
developments.why_it_matters: You can now scale AI‑agent development to dozens of concurrent sessions without upgrading your hardware, saving time and avoiding laptop overheating.
